High Court Of Madhya Pradesh

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Shri Dhanraj Singh Choudhary, counsel for the petitioners.

Shri Sourabh Shrivastava, Deputy Govt. Adv. for the
 respondent/State.

The petitioners allegedly have been implicated as accused on the complaint of Food Inspector for
offence under Section 16(1)(a)(i) read with Section 7(1) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act,
1954.
As per the prosecution story, the petitioner is running Hotel Avtar, where an inspection was carried out by the Food Inspector.
During inspection of kitchen, samples of pulses was taken.
One sample was sent to the Food Laboratory for analysis and other samples were deposited with the local Health Officer, Jabalpur.
The report of Food Laboratory dated 02.09.2011 indicates that the sample was adulterated.
Therefore, there is violation of Section 7(1) and 16(1)(a)(i) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954.

The order impugned has been conceded, wherein the application for impleading Neetu Kirana and General Store, Utsav Hotel Complex, Russel Chowk, Jabalpur, wherefrom, allegedly the pulses has been purchased, has been dismissed on the ground that the bill does not contain any batch number.
Keeping in view the aforesaid, the petition is dismissed.

However, the petitioner is granted liberty to file appropriate application before the learned trial Court under the provisions of Cr.P.C.
C.C. as per rules.

SUSHIL KUMAR PALO) JUDGE vkt Shri Arvind Supan Kumar vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 August, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/48095561/
